Females of this species attain a maximum adult body mass of 12.1 grams [Wwi = 12.1 grams] during the breeding season, while males reach a slightly higher ultimate wet weight of 12.8 grams [Wwi = 12.8 grams], a pattern of sexual size dimorphism noted in several woodcreeper lineages. These adult masses are comparatively low for a bird of this foraging guild, possibly reflecting the energetic constraints of an insectivorous diet pursued through bark-gleaning.

The species occupies a broad geographic range spanning from southern Mexico to northern Argentina, occupying both lowland and foothill forests. Foraging observations reveal that Sittasomus griseicapillus primarily consumes ants, beetles, and spiders extracted from bark crevices, with a peak feeding rate that can exceed 20 prey items per hour during the early morning. Vocalizations consist of a series of high-pitched descending notes that serve in territory advertisement and pair contact, and are most frequently emitted at dawn. Habitat preferences include mature forest interiors as well as selectively logged stands, though local densities decline sharply in heavily deforested landscapes. The species overlaps in range with larger congeners, but competitive interactions appear minimal given differences in prey size selection and substrate usage.
